introHeading: The GIF booth for Queens' biggest guest lists
introParas: Queens throws the biggest guest lists we see all year — multigenerational weddings that fill a catering hall in Astoria, Sweet Sixteens with two hundred people on the list, company parties in Long Island City spaces with enough ceiling height for a party twice the size. Big crowds change what you want from a booth: throughput matters more than novelty, and the GIF booth is built for exactly that. A burst of frames becomes a finished, shareable loop in seconds, so a line doesn't back up the way it would around a slower rig.

Every session includes stills and boomerangs alongside the GIF, and a branded overlay goes on all of them — a monogram and date for a Forest Hills wedding, a school crest for a Flushing graduation party, a company logo for an LIC office opening. Guests get everything sent straight to their phone by text, email or QR code before they've walked back to the table.

The footprint stays compact — 10ft x 10ft is ideal, 8ft x 8ft works, and it needs only a standard outlet within 15 feet, which fits inside even a packed catering hall floor plan. If your guest count is large enough that one booth will still mean a wait, ask us about pairing it with a roaming attendant to cover the room faster. Queens is a standard service area with no surprise fees — travel is quoted from your venue ZIP code before you book — and we're out across Astoria, Flushing, Long Island City, Forest Hills, Jamaica and Ridgewood most weekends.

faqHeading: GIF Photo Booth in Queens — FAQ

faqs.q: Will the GIF booth keep up with a big catering hall guest list?
faqs.a: That's what it's built for. A GIF renders in seconds rather than the longer wait a print-only booth can create, so a line at a two-hundred-guest Astoria wedding keeps moving instead of backing up during the reception.

faqs.q: Can we pair the GIF booth with a roaming attendant for a large wedding?
faqs.a: Yes, and it's a common pairing for bigger Queens guest lists. The GIF booth anchors one spot and draws a crowd, while a roaming attendant covers the seated tables and cocktail area who'd otherwise never queue.

faqs.q: Is there a travel fee for the GIF booth in Queens?
faqs.a: No surprise fees. Queens is a standard service area, and travel is quoted from your venue ZIP code before you book.

faqs.q: Does the GIF booth fit in a Long Island City loft or gallery space?
faqs.a: Easily. It's one of our most compact rigs at 10ft x 10ft ideal and 8ft x 8ft workable, so it sits comfortably in an LIC loft without competing for floor space with the rest of your setup.

faqs.q: How much space and power does the GIF booth need?
faqs.a: 10ft x 10ft is ideal, 8ft x 8ft is workable, and we need a standard 110V, 5-amp, 3-prong outlet within 15 feet — straightforward for most Queens catering hall floor plans.

faqs.q: Is an attendant included with the rental?
faqs.a: Yes. A trained attendant runs the booth for the full length of your rental — setup, keeping the prop table organized, helping guests, and pack-down afterward.

About 20 minutes from walk-in to first shot. We arrive a full hour before your scheduled start so everything is tested and ready before guests arrive. If you need us on site earlier than that, idle time runs at $150 per hour.

faqs.q: Do you carry insurance for Queens catering halls that require a COI?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million liability insurance policy, and most catering halls in Astoria and Flushing are used to receiving one — send us their contact details and we'll get it sent over.
